suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.example: A $150 ceremony meeting (1 hour). A card is saved for the studio's $25 late-cancel fee. Alex pays at the studio.

suggested_services.example: A custom ceremony quoted after the free first call: $600, with a $150 deposit now and the $450 rest on the bill after the ceremony.

before_times: What it's for: a wedding, a small or elopement ceremony, a vow renewal, or a custom ceremony
The date and the start time, and how long the ceremony should run
Where: a venue, a home, a park or the studio, and the town only (for the travel fee)
How many guests, and indoors, outdoors, or both (an outdoor ceremony has a weather rule)
Whether they want a rehearsal, extra time, or a custom ceremony
after_time: The couple's names as they'll be read, and how each wants to be introduced
Whether they'll write their own vows, use a set text, or both (the ceremony form)
The readings, music cues and who gives or walks with whom, on the ceremony form
The venue's contact and mobile, and the venue's rules (start time, the spot to stand, the sound, the curfew)
secure_page_only: The venue's gate or door codes
Anyone in the ceremony under 18 (a ring bearer or flower child): a parent's yes, and the parent stays
A health or access need of anyone in the ceremony (a bedside, a hospice, or a wheelchair near the front)
A family note, like guests to keep apart
The marriage license number, where the county issues one, and the date it was issued
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. Either partner may book, and both sign the ceremony agreement. Anyone booking for someone else says they have that person's yes. Nobody under the state's age to marry may be booked.

stop.words: Someone says they are being made to marry, or is scared to say no
stop.says: If you are in danger now, call 911. No ceremony is booked here.
stop.booking: No booking. The owner gets a plain note that a booking was stopped for safety, with no names or details.

stop.words: Someone under the state's age to marry is named as one of the couple
stop.says: A ceremony can't go ahead for anyone under the state's age to marry.
stop.booking: No booking, and the owner is told in plain words, with no names.

stop.words: Someone can't say what they want, or says they didn't agree
stop.says: The officiant can't go ahead until each person says yes in their own words.
stop.booking: No booking until each person has answered for themselves.

go_on.words: Someone at the ceremony faints, or can't breathe, or has a health emergency
go_on.says: Call 911 now if it's serious. The ceremony stops, and help comes first.
go_on.booking: The ceremony stops; the owner is told. The owner decides what's kept; Rosie makes no new charge.

go_on.words: Fire, smoke or a gas smell at the venue on the day
go_on.booking: The ceremony moves or stops; the owner decides with the couple.

safety_and_stop_words.always: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first. Rosie never judges a situation: the officiant or the owner decides.

prep: The final ceremony form, 2 days before
The officiant's arrival time and where to park
A spot to stand, and a sound check if the venue sets one
Each guest's seat, from the couple's own list

staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each officiant's credential where the state asks for one, as the business says it; nothing is looked up.
staff.supervision: A new officiant works with a lead officiant the owner names, where the state's rules allow.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs every custom quote, any stand-in officiant and any extra time added on the day.
staff.stand_in: On location: another officiant the couple accepts, offered by name; the agreement names the stand-in, so with no reply by 8pm the evening before, the stand-in comes and the owner calls. A full refund is always the other choice. The stand-in gets the ceremony form and the venue's rules, nothing else.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. Either partner may book, and both sign the ceremony agreement. Anyone booking for someone else says they have that person's yes. Nobody under the state's age to marry may be booked.
children_and_age.minors_texts: A ring bearer or flower child under 18 is named only on the secure page; a parent's yes, and the parent stays. Rosie never texts a minor first.
children_and_age.minors_rules: A parent's yes for anyone under 18 named in the ceremony, and the parent stays.

visit.done: The officiant texts DONE when the ceremony is over and the signed papers are with the couple or the county's office.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: No state license to perform a wedding in most places. Many states ask an officiant to hold a credential: an ordination, a registration with the county, or a state officiant's card. The state's form says which applies; the business says what it holds.
license.who: Each officiant holds their own credential where the state asks for one. The business holds any business license or registration. Ceremonies at a venue follow the venue's own rules.
ask: The officiant's credential, where the state's form asks for one (the business writes it in its own words)
The business license or registration number, where the city or county asks for one
The liability insurance policy and its end date, if a venue asks
license.insurance: Liability insurance on file, with its end date, where a venue asks. Many venues ask for a certificate naming them.
license.background: Only where a venue or the state's form asks. The business's own word, never checked by Rosie.

never_in_a_text: Health, access and family notes, the venue's codes, any minor's name, and anything about a ceremony that could hurt someone stay on the secure page and the officiant's job link, never in a text to the couple, the owner or the staff. A text says only 'a note is on the page'.
